title: Prime Minister congratulates people of Chhattisgarh for special celebration of ‘Bastar Pandum’ festival
content:
Press Release:Press Information Bureau Prime Minister's Office Prime Minister congratulates people of Chhattisgarh for special celebration of ‘Bastar Pandum’ festival Posted On:
                10 FEB 2026 10:42AM by PIB Delhi The Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi has congratulated the people of Chhattisgarh for special celebration of ‘Bastar Pandum’ festival, between February 7 and 9 in Chhattisgarh. During the festival, the rich culture, traditions, and tribal heritage of Bastar were showcased in a magnificent way. Shri Modi stated that such events play a vital role in preserving our cultural heritage and empowering local communities. "Earlier, whenever the name of Bastar was mentioned, images of Maoism, violence, and backwardness in development would come to mind. But now the situation has completely changed. Today, Bastar is known not only for its development but also for the growing self-confidence of its local people. My only wish is that the coming time for this region be filled with the spirit of peace, progress, and cultural pride", Shri Modi stated. Responding to a post by Union Minister, Shri Amit  Shah on X, Shri Modi said: "7 से 9 फरवरी के बीच छत्तीसगढ़ में ‘बस्तर पंडुम’ का विशेष आयोजन किया गया। इस उत्सव के दौरान बस्तर की समृद्ध संस्कृति, परंपरा और जनजातीय विरासत का भव्य रूप दिखा। इस प्रयास से जुड़े अपने सभी परिवारजनों को मेरी हार्दिक बधाई। ऐसे आयोजन हमारी सांस्कृतिक विरासत को संरक्षित करने और स्थानीय समुदायों को सशक्त बनाने में अहम भूमिका निभाते हैं। पहले जब बस्तर का नाम लिया जाता था तो माओवाद, हिंसा और विकास में पिछड़ेपन की छवि उभरती थी। लेकिन अब हालात बिल्कुल बदल चुके हैं। आज बस्तर विकास के साथ-साथ स्थानीय लोगों के बढ़ते आत्मविश्वास के लिए जाना जाता है। मेरी यही कामना है कि यहां का आने वाला समय शांति, प्रगति और सांस्कृतिक गौरव की भावना से परिपूर्ण हो।" 7 से 9 फरवरी के बीच छत्तीसगढ़ में ‘बस्तर पंडुम’ का विशेष आयोजन किया गया। इस उत्सव के दौरान बस्तर की समृद्ध संस्कृति, परंपरा और जनजातीय विरासत का भव्य रूप दिखा। इस प्रयास से जुड़े अपने सभी परिवारजनों को मेरी हार्दिक बधाई। ऐसे आयोजन हमारी सांस्कृतिक विरासत को संरक्षित करने और… https://t.co/dG30w413C6 pic.twitter.com/200UqiFcWi — Narendra Modi (@narendramodi) February 10, 2026 *** MJPS/VJ (Release ID: 2225672) Visitor Counter : 264 Read this release in: Assamese , Urdu , Marathi , हिन्दी , Manipuri , Gujarati , Kannada , Malayalam Prime Minister's Office Prime Minister congratulates people of Chhattisgarh for special celebration of ‘Bastar Pandum’ festival Posted On:

title: India Designated Country of the Year at BIOFACH 2026, Germany
content:
Press Release:Press Information Bureau Ministry of Commerce & Industry India Designated Country of the Year at BIOFACH 2026, Germany APEDA to Highlight India’s Organic Agriculture at BIOFACH 2026 India Country Pavilion to Showcase Organic Rice, Spices, Oilseeds, Herbs and Value-Added Products Participation from Over 20 States and UTs to Highlight India’s Agricultural Diversity Posted On:
                10 FEB 2026 11:58AM by PIB Delhi India has been designated as the Country of the Year at BIOFACH 2026, the world’s leading trade fair for organic products, scheduled to be held from 10th to 13th February 2026 at Nuremberg, Germany. The Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA), under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India, is organising India’s participation at BIOFACH 2026 with a prominent and high-impact presence. India’s participation will highlight the country’s rich agricultural heritage and its strength as a major global supplier of organic products. BIOFACH Germany is the world’s largest and most influential exhibition dedicated exclusively to organic food and agriculture. APEDA has been participating in BIOFACH for more than a decade and has consistently maintained a strong presence at the event. India’s participation at BIOFACH 2026 marks a significant scale-up compared to previous editions, reflecting the expanding footprint of Indian organic exports, increased global demand for organic products, and growing participation from exporters, associations, and Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs). After a span of 14 years, India’s organic farming sector is set to take centre stage once again at BIOFACH 2026. The India Country Pavilion, set up by APEDA, will span an area of 1,074 square metres and will feature 67 co-exhibitors, including exporters of organic products, Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs), cooperatives, organic laboratories, state government organisations, and commodity boards. The pavilion will showcase a wide range of organic products such as rice, oilseeds, herbs, spices, pulses, cashew, ginger, turmeric, large cardamom, cinnamon, mango puree, and essential oils, among others. Exhibitors from more than 20 States and Union Territories are participating in the India Pavilion, reflecting the country’s vast agricultural and regional diversity. These include Assam, Meghalaya, Manipur, Delhi, Gujarat, Haryana, Karnataka, Kerala, West Bengal, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Arunachal Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, and Uttarakhand. The participation highlights region-specific organic produce and value-added food products, demonstrating India’s year-on-year expansion in international organic trade engagement. In addition to product displays, visitors to the India Pavilion will be offered curated food tastings showcasing the flavours and aromas of Indian organic products. Live sampling of aromatic biryani prepared using premium organic basmati rice and spices will be organised. Further, five GI-tagged rice varieties, namely Indrayani rice, Navara rice, Gobindbhog rice, Red rice, and Chak Hao (Black rice), will be served to visitors to highlight India’s heritage rice varieties. APEDA has also undertaken extensive branding and high-impact promotional activities at prominent locations across the Nuremberg Messe Exhibition Centre, as part of India’s designation as Country of the Year at BIOFACH 2026. As global attention increasingly shifts towards sustainability and environmentally responsible lifestyles, India’s participation as Country of the Year at BIOFACH 2026 reinforces its position as a global leader in organic agriculture. India remains committed to supplying high-quality, sustainably produced organic products that meet international standards. APEDA continues to support Indian exporters through focused initiatives aimed at enhancing their global competitiveness and strengthening India’s position as the organic food basket of the world. *** Abhishek Dayal/ Garima Singh/ Ishita Biswas (Release ID: 2225710) Visitor Counter : 181 Ministry of Commerce & Industry India Designated Country of the Year at BIOFACH 2026, Germany APEDA to Highlight India’s Organic Agriculture at BIOFACH 2026 India Country Pavilion to Showcase Organic Rice, Spices, Oilseeds, Herbs and Value-Added Products Participation from Over 20 States and UTs to Highlight India’s Agricultural Diversity Posted On:

title: Ramayana and Buddhist Circuits in Uttar Pradesh
content:
Press Release:Press Information Bureau Ministry of Tourism Ramayana and Buddhist Circuits in Uttar Pradesh Posted On:
                10 FEB 2026 11:57AM by PIB Delhi Development and promotion of tourism destinations and products including destination planning is primarily undertaken by the concerned State Government (SG)/Union Territory Administration (UTA). In order to complement the efforts of tourism infrastructure development in the country, Ministry of Tourism launched its Swadesh Darshan scheme (SDS) in 2014-15 and sanctioned 76 projects for Rs.5290.33 Crore under identified thematic circuits including Ramayana Circuit and Buddhist Circuit . The projects sanctioned under Swadesh Darshan scheme in Ramayana and Buddhist Circuits in the State of Uttar Pradesh are physically complete. The details of projects sanctioned in the State of Uttar Pradesh under various thematic circuits including Ramayana and Buddhist Circuits in Swadesh Darshan Scheme is annexed. Government of India under its ‘Special Assistance to States for Capital Investment (SASCI) – Development of Iconic Tourist Centres to Global Scale’ scheme, has also sanctioned projects in the country with the primary objective to comprehensively develop iconic tourist centres in the country, branding and marketing them at global scale. Under this scheme, the project ‘Integrated Buddhist Tourism Development in Shrawasti’ has been sanctioned in 2024-25 for Rs.80.24 Crore. This information was given by Union Minister for Tourism and Culture Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat in a written reply in Lok Sabha on 9 th February 2026. **** Sunil Kumar Tiwari tourism4pib[at]gmail[dot]com ANNEXURE Details of projects sanctioned under Swadesh Darshan Scheme in the State of Uttar Pradesh Sl. title: Tourism Projects under Swadesh Darshan and PRASHAD in Uttar Pradesh
content:
Press Release:Press Information Bureau Ministry of Tourism Tourism Projects under Swadesh Darshan and PRASHAD in Uttar Pradesh Posted On:
                10 FEB 2026 11:55AM by PIB Delhi The Ministry of Tourism through its ongoing schemes of ‘Pilgrimage Rejuvenation and Spiritual, Heritage Augmentation Drive (PRASHAD)’, Swadesh Darshan and ‘Challenge Based Destination Development (CBDD)’ – a sub-scheme of Swadesh Darshan, complements the efforts of the State Governments (SGs)/UT Administrations (UTs) by extending financial assistance to them for developing tourism related infrastructure in the country, including the State of Uttar Pradesh and National Capital Region (NCR). The projects under these schemes are implemented by the respective States/UTs. However, the Ministry of Tourism regularly monitors the progress of the projects and also encourages respective State Government/ UT Administrations to complete the projects in a time bound manner. The details of the projects sanctioned in Uttar Pradesh and National Capital Region (NCR) along with their status under the Schemes of PRASHAD , Swadesh Darshan (SD), Swadesh Darshan 2.0 and Challenge Based Destination Development (CBDD), are given in the Annexure. No proposal is under consideration of the Ministry of Tourism for development of historic Dudheshwar Nath Temple in Ghaziabad. However, receiving proposals from the State Governments/UT Administrations for financial assistance for tourism projects is a continuous process. The proposals received are examined with reference to the prescribed guidelines and financial assistance is extended for such projects subject to fulfilment of the stipulated conditions and availability of funds. The Ministry of Tourism as part of its ongoing endeavour promotes various tourism destinations and products of the country including Buddhist sites through promotional activities such as events, website, social media promotions, fairs and festivals, etc. This information was given by Union Minister for Tourism and Culture Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat in a written reply in Lok Sabha on 9 th February 2026. **** Sunil Kumar Tiwari tourism4pib[at]gmail[dot]com ANNEXURE List of projects sanctioned in Uttar Pradesh and NCR under PRASHAD Scheme Sr. No State Name of the Project Sanction Year Amount Sanctioned (₹ in Crore) 1. ministry: Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers - Department of Pharmaceuticals
title: Research projects under PRIP scheme
content:
Press Release:Press Information Bureau Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers : Department of Pharmaceuticals Research projects under PRIP scheme Posted On:
                10 FEB 2026 12:53PM by PIB Delhi T he Department of Pharmaceuticals has established seven Centres of Excellence (CoEs), one each at seven NIPERs, under Component A of the Promotion of Research & Innovation in MedTech Sector (PRIP) scheme. A total amount of ₹183.46 crore has been released for setting up these centres till 31.1.2026. A total of 710 research projects, were received from industry, start-ups and MSMEs by the closing date of 19.11.2025, including projects in priority areas that are eligible for higher financial support under the PRIP scheme. Approval for financial assistance under the scheme, including full funding assistance and higher funding assistance to eligible projects is provided after a multi-stage appraisal process, as prescribed under the scheme guidelines. This information was given by Union Minister of State for Chemicals and Fertilizers, Smt. Anupriya Patel, in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today. *** GS/PM (Release ID: 2225734) Visitor Counter : 21 Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers : Department of Pharmaceuticals Research projects under PRIP scheme Posted On:

ministry: Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers - Department of Pharmaceuticals
title: 803 Jan Aushadhi Kendras set up in Odisha
content:
Press Release:Press Information Bureau Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers : Department of Pharmaceuticals 803 Jan Aushadhi Kendras set up in Odisha Posted On:
                10 FEB 2026 12:52PM by PIB Delhi No proposal to set up Jan Aushadhi Vans to improve medicine access in tribal and flood-prone districts has been received from Government of Odisha. However, till 31.12.2025, 803 Jan Aushadhi Kendras have been opened in the State of Odisha including 21 Jan Aushadhi Kendras opened in Government premises. Further, under Rule 64 of the Drug & Cosmetic Act 1940, rule 1945, a retail license for the sale of drugs is granted for a specific, fixed premise that complies with prescribed infrastructure and storage requirements, including cold chain maintenance for life-saving drugs. Current regulations do not provide for the issuance of retail licenses to mobile units. This information was given by Union Minister of State for Chemicals and Fertilizers, Smt. Anupriya Patel, in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today. *** GS/PM (Release ID: 2225733) Visitor Counter : 24 Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers : Department of Pharmaceuticals 803 Jan Aushadhi Kendras set up in Odisha Posted On:
